methodological_rigor.justification: This is a single-center retrospective cohort (July 2019–December 2020) comparing two non-randomized treatment groups (Endostar + docetaxel HIPEC, n=25; Endostar + cisplatin HIPEC, n=23) with eligibility criteria and a clearly described HIPEC/Endostar schedule. Outcomes are defined (ORR/DCR by CR/PR/SD/PD, KPS improvement, and ascites control time), but the design is vulnerable to indication bias and residual confounding, and the authors note that key confounders (e.g., peritoneal cancer index, baseline renal function) were unavailable. Statistical methods are generally appropriate for the data types (Kaplan-Meier/log-rank for ascites control time; t-test/Wilcoxon and chi-square/Fisher for comparisons), but the small sample and sparse events limited inference, and multivariable models reportedly failed to converge.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study is a retrospective, non-randomized comparison of two intraperitoneal chemotherapy regimens for malignant ascites in peritoneal metastases, which corresponds to Oxford LoE 4 (low-quality observational cohort/case series). The question is clinically relevant because malignant ascites is a high-burden complication and the manuscript evaluates patient-centered and safety endpoints (KPS improvement, ascites control time, and adverse reactions including renal impairment). The main efficacy outcomes were similar between groups while nephrotoxicity differed, providing actionable safety information for regimen selection in high-risk patients.

reporting_quality.justification: As a retrospective observational cohort, STROBE is the most applicable reporting standard. The manuscript reports inclusion/exclusion criteria, treatment procedures (Endostar dosing days and HIPEC temperature/duration description), endpoint definitions, and the statistical tests used, but important elements for observational causal interpretation are limited (non-random treatment assignment, missing key confounders, and failed multivariable adjustment due to sparsity). No data or code sharing statement or repository accessions are provided in the blinded text, so reproducibility is limited to the narrative methods.

novelty_literature.justification: The work applies a combined intraperitoneal Endostar plus HIPEC approach and directly compares docetaxel versus cisplatin within this setting, with an emphasized renal-toxicity signal for cisplatin. However, the manuscript positions this as building on prior reports of Endostar in serous effusions and HIPEC in peritoneal disease rather than introducing a new therapeutic class or definitive comparative trial. Given the small retrospective design and incremental comparative framing, the novelty is meaningful but not field-defining.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is organized in a standard clinical format with a quantitatively grounded abstract (sample sizes, ORR/DCR, median ascites control times, and key adverse-event differences). Methods sections provide concrete eligibility criteria and a stepwise description of the HIPEC procedure and dosing schedule, and results are presented with clear group comparisons and P-values. Limitations are explicitly discussed (sample size, missing confounders, retrospective bias), supporting interpretability.

key_strengths: Direct head-to-head comparison of two commonly used HIPEC agents (docetaxel vs cisplatin) under the same Endostar-based protocol with defined endpoints (ORR/DCR, KPS, ascites control time).
Adverse event reporting identifies a clinically relevant safety difference (higher renal impairment in the cisplatin group).
Limitations are explicitly acknowledged, including sparsity that prevented multivariable adjustment and unmeasured confounding.
key_concerns: Retrospective, non-randomized treatment assignment with key confounders unavailable (e.g., peritoneal cancer index and baseline renal function), limiting causal claims.
Small sample size (48 total) and sparse outcomes reduce power to detect efficacy differences and lead to unstable adjusted analyses.
No clear data/code availability information, limiting independent reproducibility.
chief_reviewer.rationale: The study addresses an important palliative-care question and provides a plausible safety signal, but the small retrospective design and missing confounding control make it more appropriate for a low-tier clinical journal and would require substantial revision to strengthen causal interpretation and reporting completeness.
